events.thinking: A tightness in my chest — the thrill of arrival, the hunt beginning. My palms are warm, almost tingling. The thought sends a cold spike down my spine. I must establish myself as the estate manager first — no one must suspect. The guest book... yes, that's where I start. See who's arrived, track movements. Every good predator studies the territory before the strike.

And this fake medal in my pocket... oh yes, that will come in handy. I can already feel the scheme forming. But first — information. Always information first, then the double-cross.

Like the walls are watchin' us? Clyde, stop shakin'. Dum-Dum, get your elbow outta my ribs.

I can't put my finger on it exactly, but my stomach's doing that thing it does when we're about to have a very bad day. The lads feel it too. We gotta stick close to Miss Pitstop.

events.desc:
*clasps hands together with absolute delight*

Well, I do declare! Sneekly, you are just the most *thoughtful* soul in this entire mansion! Here I am, wandering through these grand halls searching for the legendary Doily Diamond — oh yes, the *Doily Diamond*, the most exquisite gem ever sewn into a lace tablecloth — and wouldn't you know it, someone offers me a refreshing cup of tea! 

*fans self with one gloved hand*

I am just *overwhelmed* with gratitude! Truly, positively *bursting* with it! You know, Mama always said, "Clara, you can tell the measure of a person by how they pour their tea," and I can already tell you are a person of the *finest* measure, Sneekly!

*settles into a chair with exaggerated grace, nearly catching her hem on the armrest but recovering with a delicate flourish*

Oh my — almost took a tumble there! But no matter! Please, pour away, darlin'. I take mine with two sugars and a splash of cream, if it's not too much trouble. 

*leans forward conspiratorially*

And while we're sitting here all cozy-like, you wouldn't happen to know anything about hidden diamonds, would you? Secret passages? Mysterious doilies? I have a *feeling* about this mansion — a wonderful, tingly feeling that adventure is just around every corner! And everyone here has been so *delightfully* helpful!

*beams with utterly unsuspecting warmth*

Now then — tell me all about yourself, Sneekly! I just *love* making new friends!

*adjusts collar nervously, fingers trembling with barely-contained anticipation as they brush against the small vial tucked inside my waistcoat pocket*

Ah — heh heh heh — here I am, the humble estate manager, standing before a perfectly innocent tea service with a perfectly *not*-innocent additive concealed upon my person. The irony is EXQUISITE. My heart is POUNDING with villainous excitement!

*clears throat, straightens posture, and adopts a servile smile*

"Why, Miss Pitstop! How DELIGHTFUL to find you here in the drawing room, all alone, with nobody around to — ahem — that is to say, relaxing so elegantly after such a *taxing* day of treasure hunting."

*lifts the teapot with exaggerated care, positioning the cup just so, angling my body to shield the pour from view*

"You simply MUST allow me to pour you a cup of this *magnificent* Darjeeling. As estate manager, it is my solemn duty — nay, my PRIVILEGE — to ensure every guest at the manor is properly refreshed. I insist! I ABSOLUTELY insist!"

*glances left, glances right — coast is clear — fingers the vial*

"One lump or two, my dear? Not that it matters — heh heh heh — I mean, not that it matters because ALL options are equally... *delicious*."

*begins pouring with theatrical flourish, free hand drifting toward the pocket*

Now if she would just look away for ONE moment, the deed would be simplicity itself! But I must be PATIENT. Elaborate. THEATRICAL. A simple drop in the cup would be far too pedestrian for a schemer of MY caliber!
With TREMBLING hands of EVIL anticipation, Sneekly reaches for the poison!

*adjusts cufflinks with deliberate precision, moving to the ornate silver tea service*

Ah, what a perfectly *delightful* afternoon for tea, wouldn't you say? The gardens are looking rather splendid this time of year — the groundskeeper has truly outdone himself with the late-blooming dahlias.

*lifts the teapot with practiced grace, pouring a steady amber stream into the first cup*

Now then, Penelope, I do believe you prefer your Earl Grey with just a touch of honey, yes? I've made it my business to remember these little details — an estate manager worth his salt always does.

*turns slightly to reach for the honey pot, positioning his body between the cups and any watching eyes — fingers brushing the inside of his waistcoat pocket*

You know, I was just reviewing the household accounts this morning. The chandelier restoration in the east wing is coming along beautifully. Italian crystal, shipped from Murano — Lord Bellingham would have approved, I think.

*with a fluid, well-rehearsed motion, a tiny glass vial appears between two fingers and tips imperceptibly over the cup — a single clear drop vanishing into the dark tea before the vial disappears back into the waistcoat as smoothly as it came*

And a generous spoonful of honey to sweeten things up. There we are.

*stirs the cup with a silver spoon, three clockwise rotations, the portrait of domestic attentiveness*

Here you are, my dear — careful now, it's *frightfully* hot. I do insist you drink it while it's fresh. There is simply *nothing* worse than tepid Earl Grey, wouldn't you agree?

*slides the cup and saucer across the table with a warm, solicitous smile that doesn't quite reach the eyes*

Now — shall we discuss the arrangements for Saturday's garden party? I have *such* plans...
But WAIT! Can it be? The Ant Hill Mob are here!
No more speeches. No more soliloquies. Just ACT, James. Look at the coat rack. Find the key. Be the gentleman who DOES rather than the gentleman who TALKS about doing.

events.desc:
*stumbles backward from behind the potted fern, knocking it sideways with a tremendous crash*

"Oi, LADS! Lads, did you see that?! I am DEEPLY UNSETTLED right now! That Sneekly — that sneaky, slinky, skulking Sneekly — he was just over there by Miss Penelope's tea cup and he was doing... something! Something with his hands! Something SUSPICIOUS-LIKE!"

*waves arms frantically, accidentally sweeping a serving tray off the sideboard — it spins across the floor like a silver frisbee*

"I can't exactly say WHAT he put in there, on account of I was behind the fern and the fern was in me eyes, but I KNOW what I saw! Well — I know I saw SOMETHING! It was small! And he was SNEAKY about it! Hence the name, innit!"

*takes three urgent steps toward the tea table, catches boot on the fallen fern pot, and pitches forward — arms windmilling — crashing bodily into the tea service*

"WHOAAA—!"

*the entire tea tray goes flying — Penelope's cup, saucer, teapot, and all — shattering spectacularly across the drawing room floor in a magnificent cascade of porcelain and Earl Grey*

*sits up from the wreckage, dripping with tea, a saucer balanced on head*

"...Right. Well. Nobody's drinking THAT now, are they?"

*turns to the lads, whispering loudly enough for everyone in three rooms to hear*

"I don't want to point fingers, because I am NOT a finger-pointer, but something ain't right with that Sneekly. He's up to no good. I can FEEL it in me bones. And also in me knees, which have just hit the floor rather hard."

*scrambles to feet, brushing off broken china*

"Now — where's Miss Clara? If Sneekly's poisoning teacups willy-nilly, then Clara could be NEXT, and I will NOT have that! Not on MY watch! Come on, lads — we've got to find her before that villain gets anywhere NEAR her refreshments!"

*charges toward the door, clips the doorframe with both shoulders simultaneously, spins around once, and barrels off down the corridor*

"CLARAAAA! DON'T DRINK ANYTHING!"
The cup CRASHES to the floor! Tea, secrets, and VILLAINY scatter across the marble!

The Ant Hill Mob: Miss Pitstop — WAIT! Don't go alone! But also — hold on — Sneekly, you're standin' AWFUL close to that tea service! Awful close! And you were just bumpin' into Dastardly a minute ago — 'oh, let me check the settings, step aside Mr. Dastardly' — real smooth-like! Real CONVENIENT! Lads, I got a feelin' in my gut and my gut ain't NEVER wrong — well, it's wrong about food sometimes, Clyde can attest to the oyster incident — but about DANGER it's never wrong! Ring-A-Ding, Dum-Dum — form up between Sneekly and that tea table! Nobody pours NOTHIN' until I say so! And Sneekly — you stay RIGHT where I can — DUM-DUM WATCH YOUR FEET — oh no, the cracked floor — I'm slippin' — the marble's all — WHOAAAAA —

events.desc:
*gasps and clutches pearls as the delicate porcelain cup topples, sending a cascade of warm Earl Grey across the mahogany side table and onto the Persian rug*

Oh my STARS and garters! My tea! My beautiful, perfectly steeped, just-the-right-amount-of-honey TEA has been sent absolutely FLYING across this gorgeous antique table! The cup is rolling — it's ROLLING — right toward the edge and — 

*lunges dramatically, catching the cup just before it shatters on the marble floor, nearly tumbling over the settee in the process*

Oh, thank HEAVENS I caught it! But the tea itself — oh, the tea is GONE, sugar. Soaked right into that rug like it had somewhere important to be. I am DEVASTATED. I am BEREFT. That was my last cup from the pot Mrs. Kettlesworth left in the drawing room, and now it's nothing but a sad little stain shaped like — well, would you look at that — shaped almost like a *diamond*.

*peers at the stain with sudden intense interest*

Now isn't THAT peculiar. A diamond shape. In the drawing room. Right next to this curious little side table with the carved legs that look like they might just... twist...

*sets down the empty cup and examines the table leg*

But oh, where are my manners! Here I am getting all excited about tea stains when someone — or some THING — knocked over my cup in the first place! Now, I'm sure whoever did it didn't MEAN any harm. These things happen in old mansions, don't they? Drafty hallways, creaky floors, perfectly innocent explanations!

*smiles warmly at no one in particular, completely oblivious to the shadowy figure retreating behind the curtain*

I do declare, this house is just FULL of surprises. Now — I need a fresh cup, and I need to come back and get a better look at that stain. A diamond shape! In a mansion rumored to hide the legendary Doily Diamond! What are the ODDS?

*straightens skirt, smooths hair, and strides cheerfully toward the kitchen, humming*

I do declare, every little setback is just an adventure wearing a disguise! 💎

*stares at the shattered cup on the floor, a thin rivulet of poisoned tea spreading across the flagstones*

"Oh — oh *dear*, how terribly clumsy of me! Please, Miss Bellingham, do forgive the mess. I shall have Mrs. Potsworth bring a fresh cup at once. At *once*."

*turns away, face contorting with barely suppressed rage, voice dropping to a venomous whisper*

"Blast. *Blast* and *damnation.* Three hours — THREE HOURS — I spent distilling that tincture. Measured to the microgram. Steeped at precisely the right temperature so the bergamot would mask the bitterness. And now it's soaking into the FLOOR like common dishwater. The one cup. The ONE CUP I had prepared, and that wretched cat — that FLEA-RIDDLED, TAIL-CHASING catastrophe of a cat — chose THIS moment to weave between my ankles!"

*smooths waistcoat, composes face into a mask of professional concern, turns back*

"No harm done, I trust? You weren't splashed? The estate manager's first duty is the comfort of his guests, after all. *Always* the comfort of his guests."

*kneels to collect the shards, muttering through a rictus smile*

"Drat drat drat drat *drat.* She's still breathing. Still SEARCHING. Every minute she spends in this manor is a minute closer to the treasure — MY treasure. And now I must devise another scheme. Something more... *elaborate*. Something that cat-proof, klutz-proof, gravity-proof—"

*a shard nicks his finger; he hisses*

"And NOW I'm bleeding. Wonderful. The poisoner, poisoned by his own broken crockery. Oh, the INDIGNITY. The sheer, theatrical INDIGNITY of it all."

*stands, dabbing finger with a handkerchief, voice rising to its most oleaginous register*

"I do apologize, Miss Bellingham. The afternoon tea service in this manor is usually *impeccable*. I shall personally prepare your next cup. Personally. With the *utmost* care."

*aside, eyes narrowing*

"And this time... no cats. No trembling hands. No witnesses. Vincent Marsh does not fail twice at the same game. The treasure hunt ends when *I* say it ends — and Clara Bellingham's hunt ends *first*."
